key_insight: Foundation model representations from pathology images and transcriptomics are complementary, and combining them can improve multimodal cancer classification—especially when no single modality dominates.
clinical_relevance: For oncology workflows, this suggests FM-based multimodal decision support may be more robust under real-world dataset shift, with uncertainty estimates helping flag uncertain cases.
method: Benchmarked 5 foundation models on 8 downstream classification tasks
Compared unimodal probing with 3 paired image-omics fusion strategies
evidence_signal: The study tested real-world, out-of-distribution performance on two commercial cohorts (IH-BC and IH-NSCLC) using whole-slide images and transcriptomic profiles.
watch_item: Results come from retrospective cohort evaluation, so external validation and careful integration into clinical workflows are still needed before deployment.
paper_title: Probing, Fusion, and Trustworthiness: A Systematic Evaluation of Foundation Model Representations for Multimodal Cancer Analysis
